question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

By definition, making a pictogram is to present and visualise data.
option_1: To make a pictogram by definition
option_3: In making a pictogram, the definition
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The purpose of a pictorgram.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence intends to say what a pictogram is meant for — "The purpose of a pictogram is to present and visualise data." The phrase "By definition, making a pictogram" is awkward and illogical, because it is not the act of *making* a pictogram that "is to present data"; it is the purpose/function of a pictogram.

◦ Correct: The purpose of a pictogram is to present and visualise data.

• "The purpose of X is to + verb" is a standard, natural construction to state the function of something. (किसी वस्तु का उद्देश्य बताने की मानक संरचना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "To make a pictogram by definition" keeps the same awkward structure and does not fit before "is to present ...".

• Option 2 "Pictogram is making a definition" completely distorts the meaning.

• Option 3 "In making a pictogram, the definition" leaves the sentence without a proper subject for "is to present".

NOTE

• A pictogram/pictograph is a chart that uses pictures or symbols to represent data. Remember the pattern: "The purpose/aim/objective of X is to + base verb".

question:
Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The princepal of the college announced his early retirement today.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. principal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "principal", meaning the head of a school or college. (प्रधानाचार्य)

◦ Correct: The principal of the college announced his early retirement today.

• Spelling key: PRIN + CI + PAL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "princepil", "principel" and "princeaple" are all misspelt forms.

• Memory trick: The principal is your pal (friend).

NOTE

• Do not confuse principal (head of an institution; also "main/chief", or a sum of money on which interest is calculated) with principle (a rule, law or moral standard). "The principal followed his principles."

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

It was an interesting chat with an European gymnast that changed my mindset towards the sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. an European gymnast that changed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "European" begins with the consonant sound /juː/ ("yu"), so it takes the article "a", not "an". The choice of a/an depends on the sound, not the spelling.

◦ Correct: It was an interesting chat with a European gymnast that changed my mindset towards the sport.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "It was an interesting" is correct — "interesting" begins with a vowel sound, so "an" is right there.

• "chat with" and "my mindset towards the sport" contain no error.

NOTE

• Use "a" before words with a consonant sound: a European, a university, a one-rupee coin, a useful book. Use "an" before a vowel sound: an hour, an honest man, an MLA, an umbrella. (उच्चारण के आधार पर a/an का प्रयोग)

question:
Select the most appropriate degree of comparison to fill in the blank.

Hunny is _____ person in his family.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. the tallest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When one person is compared with all the members of a group ("in his family"), the superlative degree with "the" is used — "the tallest".

◦ Correct: Hunny is the tallest person in his family.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "more taller" is a double comparative — always wrong (never combine "more" with "-er").

• Option 2 "tall" (positive degree) cannot single out one person from a group.

• Option 3 "taller" (comparative) is used to compare only two persons/things, usually with "than".

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: tall – taller (than) – the tallest (of/in a group). The superlative always takes the definite article "the": the tallest, the best, the most intelligent.

question: If someone mentions that 'the ball is in your court', what does this idiom imply?
option_2: It's your turn to make a decision or take action.
option_3: It's time to play a sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. It's your turn to make a decision or take action.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the ball is in your court" means it is now your responsibility/turn to make the next decision or take the next step. (अब निर्णय लेने की बारी आपकी है)

◦ Example: I have sent my proposal; now the ball is in your court.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Though the expression originates from court games like tennis, as an idiom it is not literally about sport — so Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "take the initiative", "make the first move", "pass the buck" (shift responsibility to someone else — the opposite idea).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Harmony
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Discord.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harmony" means agreement, peaceful coexistence and concord. Its antonym is "discord", meaning disagreement, conflict or lack of harmony. (सद्भाव का विलोम — कलह/मतभेद)

◦ Example: Constant discord among the members destroyed the harmony of the group.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Accord" (agreement), Option 3 "Unity" (oneness) and Option 4 "Concord" (agreement/harmony) are all synonyms of harmony, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of harmony: accord, concord, unity, amity, peace. Antonyms: discord, conflict, dissension, disagreement, strife.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I have been / looking by my / cream sweater for / a few weeks now.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. looking by my.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct phrasal verb is "look for", meaning to search for/try to find something. "Look by" is not a valid phrasal verb here — the segment should be "looking for my".

◦ Correct: I have been looking for my cream sweater for a few weeks now.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "I have been" (present perfect continuous) is correct with "for a few weeks now".

• "cream sweater for" and "a few weeks now" are correct.

NOTE

• Common "look" phrasal verbs: look for (search), look after (take care of), look into (investigate), look up to (respect), look forward to (await eagerly), look down upon (despise).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She _______ to be understood by the society.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sought.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sought" (past tense of "seek") means tried/attempted to obtain or achieve something. "Seek + to-infinitive" is a standard pattern: she sought to be understood = she tried to be understood. (प्रयास किया / चाहा)

◦ Correct: She sought to be understood by the society.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "chased" and Option 2 "hunted" mean physically pursuing something and do not take a to-infinitive in this sense.

• Option 4 "looked" would need "looked forward to being understood" or a different structure; "looked to be understood" is unidiomatic here.

NOTE

• Verb forms: seek – sought – sought. "Seek to do something" = attempt to do it. Similar pattern verbs: try to, attempt to, endeavour to, strive to.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. rhetericol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rhetericol" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "rhetorical", meaning relating to the art of effective speaking or writing; (of a question) asked for effect, not for an answer. (आलंकारिक/भाषण-कला संबंधी)

◦ Example: "Who doesn't want to be happy?" is a rhetorical question.

• Spelling key: RHE + TO + RI + CAL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "tangible" (that can be touched; real), "navigate" (to find one's way/steer) and "lascivious" (showing strong sexual desire; lustful) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with silent/tricky "rh": rhetoric, rhythm, rhyme, rhinoceros. The noun is rhetoric; the adjective is rhetorical.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Rain cats and dogs
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Raining heavily.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "rain cats and dogs" means to rain very heavily. (मूसलाधार वर्षा होना)

◦ Example: We could not go out because it was raining cats and dogs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Doing something pointless" suggests idioms like "flogging a dead horse".

• Option 2 "Very rarely" matches "once in a blue moon".

• Option 3 "Do something unplanned" matches "play it by ear".

NOTE

• Weather idioms: "come rain or shine" (whatever happens), "under the weather" (unwell), "a storm in a teacup" (great fuss over a small matter), "every cloud has a silver lining" (something good in every bad situation).

question:
Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Food prices in Switzerland are expensiver to the rest of Western Europe.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. more expensive than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Expensive" is a long adjective, so its comparative is formed with "more" — "more expensive", never "expensiver". The comparative degree is always followed by "than", not "to".

◦ Correct: Food prices in Switzerland are more expensive than the rest of Western Europe.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "the most expensive than" wrongly combines the superlative with "than".

• Option 3 "as expensiver to" — "expensiver" is not a word, and "as ... as" would be needed for the positive degree.

• Option 4 "more expensive to" uses the wrong particle; comparatives take "than".

NOTE

• Adjectives of two or more syllables (expensive, beautiful, intelligent) take "more ... than" (comparative) and "the most ..." (superlative). Exceptions using "to" instead of "than": senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior, preferable (senior to, superior to).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The speaker requested the audience to pay _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. attention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The fixed collocation is "pay attention", meaning to listen to/watch or consider something carefully. (ध्यान देना)

◦ Correct: The speaker requested the audience to pay attention.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• We do not say "pay ears" (the idiom is "lend an ear"), "pay silence" (we "keep/maintain silence") or "pay activeness".

NOTE

• Common collocations with "pay": pay attention, pay a visit, pay a compliment, pay respect/homage, pay heed, pay tribute, pay the price. Collocations must be learnt as fixed word-pairs for SSC exams.

question:
Which of the following options is similar in meaning to the given word?

Pensive
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Thoughtful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pensive" means engaged in deep or serious thought, often with a touch of sadness. Its closest synonym is "thoughtful". (विचारमग्न / चिंतनशील)

◦ Example: She sat in a pensive/thoughtful mood, staring out of the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Troubled" (worried/disturbed) is close in feeling but not the meaning of pensive.

• Option 2 "Talkative" (fond of talking) and Option 4 "Tired" (fatigued) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of pensive: thoughtful, reflective, contemplative, meditative, musing. Antonyms: carefree, unthinking, frivolous.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The council never _________ the new complex to be constructed, nor did local residents.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. wanted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Wanted" fits both the meaning and the grammar — "want + object + to-infinitive" is a standard pattern: "The council never wanted the new complex to be constructed". (चाहना)

◦ Correct: The council never wanted the new complex to be constructed, nor did local residents.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "occurred" (happened) makes no sense with an object.

• Option 2 "refreshed" (made fresh again) is unrelated.

• Option 4 "liked" does not idiomatically take the pattern "liked the complex to be constructed" in this negative desire sense; "wanted" is the natural verb of desire here.

NOTE

• Pattern: want/expect/would like + object + to-infinitive — "I want the work to be finished." Also note the inversion "nor did local residents" (auxiliary + subject) after a negative clause.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

How long / have you / been learn / English now?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. been learn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The present perfect continuous tense requires "have/has + been + V-ing". So "been learn" must be "been learning".

◦ Correct: How long have you been learning English now?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "How long", "have you" and "English now" are all correct.

• "How long + present perfect continuous" is the standard way to ask about the duration of an ongoing action.

NOTE

• Structure: Subject + have/has + been + verb-ing (I have been learning, she has been working). Used for actions that started in the past and are still continuing, usually with "since/for/how long".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the highlighted word in the given sentence.

The negotiations were conducted in an amicable atmosphere, leading to a peaceful resolution.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Hostile.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amicable" means friendly and without conflict. Its antonym is "hostile", meaning unfriendly, aggressive or antagonistic. (मैत्रीपूर्ण का विलोम — शत्रुतापूर्ण)

◦ Example: The amicable talks suddenly turned hostile.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Agreeable" (pleasant), Option 2 "Serene" (calm) and Option 3 "Cordial" (warm and friendly) are all close synonyms of amicable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amicable: friendly, cordial, harmonious, amiable. Antonyms: hostile, unfriendly, antagonistic, bitter. Note: amicable describes relations/settlements; amiable describes a person's nature.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Overfishing and destructive fishing practices threaten the sustainability of marine resources and ecosystems.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Indefensibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sustainability" here carries the sense of something that can be maintained, supported or defended over time. Its antonym among the options is "indefensibility" — the state of being impossible to defend, support or justify. (टिकाऊपन/समर्थनीयता का विलोम — असमर्थनीयता)

◦ Sense: What is sustainable can be upheld/maintained; what is indefensible cannot be supported at all.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Equanimity" (calmness of mind) is unrelated.

• Option 3 "Reasonableness" and Option 4 "Justifiability" lean towards the same positive side as sustainability (able to be justified), so they cannot be antonyms.

NOTE

• Root idea: sustain = to hold up/support (Latin *sustinere*); defend/defensible share the idea of upholding. Antonym pairs to remember: sustainable ↔ unsustainable/indefensible; justifiable ↔ unjustifiable.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.

A conscious understanding of the environmental issues can bring positive changes in human life.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Mindful.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conscious" means aware of and deliberately attentive to something. Its closest synonym is "mindful" (paying careful attention; aware). (सचेत / जागरूक)

◦ Example: A conscious/mindful understanding of environmental issues leads to responsible behaviour.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Mechanical" (done without thinking) and Option 2 "Reflex" (automatic, involuntary) are the opposite idea — action without awareness.

• Option 4 "Beware" is a verb meaning "be cautious of" and does not fit as a synonym of the adjective "conscious".

NOTE

• Do not confuse conscious (aware) with conscience (moral sense of right and wrong) and conscientious (hard-working and careful). Synonyms of conscious: aware, mindful, alert, cognizant.

question:
Rectify the error in the given sentence by selecting the correct spelling from the options provided.

The chord of my voilin is not tuned properly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. violin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "violin" — a four-stringed musical instrument played with a bow. (वायलिन/बेला)

◦ Correct: The chord of my violin is not tuned properly.

• Spelling key: VI + O + LIN (i before o, and it begins with "v", not "w").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "voilen", "woilin" and "wiolin" are all misspelt forms.

• A person who plays the violin is a violinist.

NOTE

• Similar tricky spellings of instruments/music words: violin, violinist, orchestra, rhythm, guitar, xylophone. Also note chord (musical notes together) vs cord (a rope/string).

question:
Select the correct option of the given sentence.

Vishnu is the more courageous than all other boys in the class.
option_1: Vishnu is much more courageous than all other boys in the class.
option_2: Vishnu is most courageous than all other boys in the class.
option_3: Vishnu is the most courageous than all other boys in the class.
option_4: Vishnu is more courageous than all other boys in the class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Vishnu is more courageous than all other boys in the class.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When "than all other/any other" is used, the comparative degree WITHOUT "the" is required — "more courageous than all other boys". The article "the" is used only with the superlative, not the comparative.

◦ Correct: Vishnu is more courageous than all other boys in the class.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 2 and 3 wrongly use the superlative "most courageous" with "than" — the superlative never takes "than".

• Option 1 "much more courageous" adds an unnecessary intensifier and changes the intended plain comparison.

NOTE

• Superlative meaning through comparative: "Vishnu is the most courageous boy in the class" = "Vishnu is more courageous than any other/all other boys in the class." Never mix "the + comparative + than".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The ship struck the iceberg "with its side" — i.e., the side of the ship was the part that made contact with the iceberg. The preposition "with" indicates the part/instrument involved in the action. (जहाज़ ने अपने पार्श्व/बगल से हिमखंड को टक्कर मारी)

◦ Correct: The ship struck the iceberg with its side while it was still moving forward.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "under" and Option 2 "above" wrongly suggest a position below/over the iceberg.

• Option 3 "beyond" (farther than) makes no sense — the ship could not strike something beyond it.

NOTE

• "Strike/hit something with + body part/object" shows the means of contact: "He struck the nail with a hammer." Historically, the Titanic's starboard (right) side scraped the iceberg on 14–15 April 1912.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. moments.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The collision damaged the ship almost instantly, so "In a few moments, six great holes were made in the steel" is the only logical choice — a "moment" is a very short period of time. (कुछ ही क्षणों में)

◦ Correct: In a few moments, six great holes were made in the steel.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "weeks", "days" and "years" are far too long — the holes were torn in the hull during the brief collision itself, not over an extended period.

NOTE

• Words for short duration: moment, instant, second, split second, twinkling of an eye. Phrase: "in a few moments" = very quickly/immediately after.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. useless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Water rushed in "not in one place, but in separate places", so closing the watertight steel doors could not stop the flooding — the doors "were therefore useless" (of no use/ineffective). (बेकार / निष्प्रभावी)

◦ Correct: The steel doors were therefore useless.

• The linking word "therefore" demands a result that follows logically from water entering at many places at once.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "painted" and "burnt" are irrelevant to flooding.

• "complete" does not express the failure of the doors to serve their purpose.

NOTE

• Synonyms of useless: futile, ineffective, of no avail, worthless. The Titanic's watertight compartments failed because water spilled over from one flooded compartment into the next.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. nothing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Since the damage was beyond repair, "Captain Smith soon understood that nothing could save the ship" — i.e., the ship was certain to sink and no measure could prevent it. (कुछ भी जहाज़ को नहीं बचा सकता था)

◦ Correct: Captain Smith soon understood that nothing could save the ship.

• This is confirmed by the next sentence — he immediately ordered a distress call (CQD), which he would do only if the ship was doomed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "enemies", "all" and "everything" would absurdly suggest that the ship could still be saved or that enemies would save it, contradicting the call for help.

NOTE

• "Nothing could save..." is a common structure of inevitability. CQD was the early Marconi distress signal; it was later replaced by SOS. The Titanic sent both CQD and SOS in 1912.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The ship struck the iceberg (1) _____ its side while it was still moving forward. In a few (2)_____, six great holes were made in the steel. Water rushed in, not in one place, but in separate places covering the Titanic hundred feet. The steel doors were therefore (3)_____ . Captain Smith soon understood that (4)______ could save the ship. He ordered the wireless officer to send out the ship’s position and the letters CQD, which is the call for help. It told the world that the Titanic was (5)_____.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. sinking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The distress call CQD "told the world that the Titanic was sinking" — going down below the surface of the water. This matches the whole passage: holes in the steel, water rushing in, and nothing able to save the ship. (डूब रहा था)

◦ Correct: It told the world that the Titanic was sinking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "victorious" (winning) and "reaching" (arriving) contradict the disaster context.

• "floating" is the opposite of what was happening — a floating ship would not need a call for help.

NOTE

• Verb: sink – sank – sunk. The RMS Titanic sank on its maiden voyage (Southampton to New York) on 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic; over 1,500 people died.

question: What is the specific field of study focused on examining extinct animals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Palaeontology.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Palaeontology" is the scientific study of fossils — the remains of extinct animals and plants preserved in rocks — to understand the history of life on the Earth. (जीवाश्म विज्ञान)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Gemology — the study of gemstones (precious and semi-precious stones).

• Economic geology — the study of earth materials (minerals, ores, fuels) that can be used for economic purposes.

• Glaciology — the study of glaciers and ice sheets.

NOTE

• Related branches: Palaeobotany (fossil plants), Palaeozoology (fossil animals), Archaeology (study of human past through material remains). Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences is located in Lucknow.

question: In which of the following years was India the host of Women's T20 World Cup Cricket?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2016.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India hosted the ICC Women's T20 World Cup (Women's World Twenty20) in 2016, held alongside the men's tournament. The final was played at Eden Gardens, Kolkata, where the West Indies won their first Women's T20 title by defeating Australia. (2016 — भारत में महिला टी20 विश्व कप)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In the same year (2016), India also hosted the Men's T20 World Cup, won by the West Indies.

• The Women's T20 World Cup began in 2009 (won by England); Australia has been the most successful team in the tournament.

NOTE

• Cricket in India is governed by the BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India); internationally by the ICC (International Cricket Council), headquartered in Dubai, UAE.

question: The All-India Kisan Sabha was founded in Lucknow in April _______ with Swami Sahjanand Saraswati as the president.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1936.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "All-India Kisan Sabha (AIKS)" was founded at the Lucknow session of the Indian National Congress in April 1936, with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as its first president. (अखिल भारतीय किसान सभा — अप्रैल 1936, लखनऊ)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• N. G. Ranga was its first general secretary; the Kisan Manifesto was issued in August 1936.

• The Congress session at Lucknow (1936) was presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The Kisan Sabha demanded abolition of zamindari, reduction of land revenue and cancellation of rural debts.

NOTE

• Swami Sahajanand Saraswati earlier led the Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929). The AIKS marked the beginning of an organised all-India peasant movement in the freedom struggle.

question:
Match the columns.

Column A (Plant Group)  |  Column B (Example)

i. Bryophyta — a. Rose

ii. Pteridophyta — b. Pine

iii. Gymnosperms — c. Mosses

iv. Angiosperms — d. Selaginella
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-d, iii-b, iv-a.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bryophyta — Mosses (i-c): non-vascular plants called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" (e.g., moss, Marchantia, Riccia).

• Pteridophyta — Selaginella (ii-d): the first plants with vascular tissue but no seeds (e.g., ferns, Selaginella, Equisetum).

• Gymnosperms — Pine (iii-b): plants with naked seeds, not enclosed in fruits (e.g., pine, deodar, Cycas).

• Angiosperms — Rose (iv-a): flowering plants whose seeds are enclosed within fruits (e.g., rose, mango, wheat).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Plant kingdom classification (as in NCERT): Thallophyta (algae) → Bryophyta → Pteridophyta → Gymnosperms → Angiosperms.

• Angiosperms are further divided into monocots (one cotyledon — wheat, maize) and dicots (two cotyledons — pea, rose).

NOTE

• "Gymnosperm" literally means "naked seed" (Greek: gymnos = naked, sperma = seed); "Angiosperm" means "enclosed seed".

question: As per the Periodic Labour Force data 2023, which of the following states recorded the highest unemployment rate in urban areas for the age group 15 years and above?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data 2023, Himachal Pradesh recorded the highest urban unemployment rate among the given states for persons aged 15 years and above. (आवधिक श्रम बल सर्वेक्षण 2023 — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The PLFS is conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI); it was launched in 2017 (replacing the earlier five-yearly Employment-Unemployment Surveys).

• PLFS measures key indicators: Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR).

NOTE

• Unemployment Rate = (Unemployed persons / Labour force) × 100. PLFS gives quarterly estimates for urban areas and annual estimates for both rural and urban areas.

question: The Sun Temple at Konark, the Khajuraho Temple in Madhya Pradesh and the recently constructed Ram Temple in Ayodhya are examples of temples designed in which style of temple architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nagara.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Sun Temple at Konark (Odisha), the Khajuraho temples (Madhya Pradesh) and the Ram Temple at Ayodhya (Uttar Pradesh) are all built in the "Nagara" style — the North Indian style of temple architecture. (नागर शैली)

• Nagara features: a curvilinear tower (shikhara) over the sanctum (garbhagriha), an amalaka and kalasha at the top, and the temple usually built on a raised platform (jagati), generally without large enclosure walls or gateways.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Dravida style (South India): pyramid-shaped vimana, huge gateway towers (gopurams), enclosed compound — e.g., Brihadeshwara Temple, Thanjavur.

• Vesara style: a hybrid of Nagara and Dravida, seen in Karnataka (Chalukya/Hoysala regions).

• The Ayodhya Ram Temple was designed by the Sompura family of architects in the Nagara style.

NOTE

• Sub-schools of Nagara: Odisha (Kalinga) — Konark, Lingaraja; Khajuraho (Chandela) — Kandariya Mahadeva; Solanki — Modhera Sun Temple.

question: Which of the following leaders died after being hit by sticks while protesting against the Simon Commission?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lala Lajpat Rai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lala Lajpat Rai" was grievously injured in a police lathi charge while leading a protest against the Simon Commission at Lahore on 30 October 1928, and died of his injuries on 17 November 1928. (लाला लाजपत राय — साइमन कमीशन विरोध)

• He famously declared: "Every blow aimed at me is a nail in the coffin of British imperialism."

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Simon Commission (1927) was boycotted because it had no Indian member; the slogan was "Simon Go Back".

• To avenge his death, Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Chandra Shekhar Azad shot police officer J. P. Saunders at Lahore (December 1928).

• Lala Lajpat Rai, known as "Punjab Kesari (Lion of Punjab)", was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio; he founded the Servants of the People Society (1921) and wrote "Unhappy India".

NOTE

• The Lal-Bal-Pal extremist trio: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal.

question: ‘NISHTHA’ stands for ____________.
option_1: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
option_2: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
option_3: National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement
option_4: National Inauguration for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Assessment
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Initiative for School Heads’ and Teachers’ Holistic Advancement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• NISHTHA = "National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement". It is the world's largest teacher-training programme, launched by the Ministry of Education (Department of School Education and Literacy) in 2019. (शिक्षकों का समग्र उन्नयन कार्यक्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NISHTHA aims to build the capacity of elementary-level teachers and school heads through integrated training on learning outcomes, pedagogy, ICT, and inclusive education.

• Later versions: NISHTHA 2.0 (secondary level, linked with NEP 2020) and NISHTHA 3.0 (foundational literacy and numeracy, linked with the NIPUN Bharat Mission).

NOTE

• Related education initiatives: Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan, PM SHRI Schools, DIKSHA portal (digital platform used for NISHTHA online training), and the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

question: Under which of the following Articles is Right to Equality mentioned?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 14-18.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Right to Equality" is enshrined in Articles 14 to 18 of the Indian Constitution (Part III — Fundamental Rights). (समानता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 14–18)

◦ Article 14 — Equality before law and equal protection of laws.

◦ Article 15 — Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

◦ Article 16 — Equality of opportunity in public employment.

◦ Article 17 — Abolition of untouchability.

◦ Article 18 — Abolition of titles.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The six Fundamental Rights: Equality (14–18), Freedom (19–22), Against Exploitation (23–24), Freedom of Religion (25–28), Cultural & Educational Rights (29–30), Constitutional Remedies (32).

• Articles 1–4 deal with the Union and its Territory (Part I).

NOTE

• Article 32 (right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights) was called the "heart and soul of the Constitution" by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

question: Who among the following appoints the Acting Chief Justice in the absence of the Chief Justice of India?
option_2: Senior most Judge of the Supreme Court
solution_text:
The correct answer is President.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 126 of the Constitution, the "President of India" appoints an Acting Chief Justice when the office of the Chief Justice of India is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform his duties. (कार्यवाहक मुख्य न्यायाधीश की नियुक्ति — राष्ट्रपति द्वारा, अनुच्छेद 126)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Related Articles: Article 124 — establishment of the Supreme Court and appointment of judges; Article 127 — appointment of ad hoc judges; Article 128 — attendance of retired judges; Article 143 — advisory jurisdiction (Presidential reference).

• Supreme Court judges hold office until the age of 65 years; they can be removed only by the process of impeachment (Article 124(4)) on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

NOTE

• By convention, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the Acting/next Chief Justice, but the formal appointing authority is the President.

question: The condition when the amount of dissolved oxygen in a water body is alarmingly decreased is called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is hypoxia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hypoxia" is the condition in which the dissolved oxygen (DO) in a water body falls to alarmingly low levels, endangering fish and other aquatic life. (जल में घुलित ऑक्सीजन की भारी कमी — हाइपोक्सिया)

• It commonly results from eutrophication — excess nutrients (nitrates/phosphates from fertilisers, sewage) cause algal blooms; when the algae decompose, bacteria consume the oxygen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Anoxia — the complete absence of oxygen (more extreme than hypoxia).

• Hypothermia — an abnormally low body temperature (unrelated to water oxygen).

• Acidification — lowering of pH (e.g., ocean acidification due to CO₂).

NOTE

• Hypoxic zones in oceans/lakes are called "dead zones". Healthy water bodies generally need dissolved oxygen above about 5–6 mg/L; BOD (Biochemical Oxygen Demand) is a key indicator of water pollution.

question: Which among the following data was used to compute the estimates in the national Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Baseline Report?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's national Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) Baseline Report, released by NITI Aayog in 2021, was computed using the data of the "National Family Health Survey (NFHS-4), 2015-16". (राष्ट्रीय बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक — NFHS-4 आँकड़े)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The national MPI measures deprivation across three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — using 12 indicators (nutrition, child & adolescent mortality, maternal health, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, bank account).

• The later MPI Progress Review 2023 used NFHS-5 (2019-21) data, showing about 13.5 crore people exited multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

• The global MPI is published by the UNDP and OPHI (Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative).

NOTE

• NFHS is conducted by the International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS), Mumbai, under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare.

question: In Union Budget 2023-24, an aspirational Blocks Programme covering how many blocks has been launched?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 500.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, the Government announced the "Aspirational Blocks Programme (ABP)" covering 500 blocks for saturation of essential government services in areas such as health, nutrition, education, agriculture, water resources, financial inclusion, skill development and basic infrastructure. (आकांक्षी ब्लॉक कार्यक्रम — 500 ब्लॉक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The programme was formally launched on 7 January 2023 and is anchored by NITI Aayog, building on the success of the Aspirational Districts Programme (2018), which covers 112 districts.

• The Union Budget 2023-24 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman; its vision was "Amrit Kaal" with Saptarishi (seven) priorities, including inclusive development and reaching the last mile.

NOTE

• The Aspirational Blocks/Districts programmes rank areas on real-time indicators through the Champions of Change dashboard, promoting competitive and cooperative federalism.

question: Padma Shri awardee (2023) Guru K Kalyanasundaram Pillai is an exponent of which of the following classical dance genres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru K. Kalyanasundaram Pillai, who received the Padma Shri in 2023, is a veteran exponent and guru of "Bharatanatyam", associated with the Thanjavur style and the Sri Rajarajeshwari Bharatha Natya Kala Mandir, Mumbai. (भरतनाट्यम — पद्म श्री 2023)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, one of the oldest, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharat Muni and the Abhinaya Darpana of Nandikeshvara; it was revived from sadir by Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Famous Bharatanatyam dancers: Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Padma Subrahmanyam, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Mallika Sarabhai.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

question: A famous hill station 'Ranikhet' is located on which mountain?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ranikhet" ("Queen's meadow") is a famous hill station in the Almora district of Uttarakhand, situated in the Kumaon Himalaya at an altitude of about 1,800 m. (रानीखेत — हिमालय, उत्तराखंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ranikhet is a cantonment town — home of the Kumaon Regiment of the Indian Army — and offers views of Himalayan peaks like Nanda Devi.

• Other Himalayan hill stations: Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital, Almora, Darjeeling.

• Hill stations of the Western Ghats: Ooty (Udagamandalam), Munnar, Mahabaleshwar, Lonavala; Aravalli: Mount Abu (Rajasthan).

NOTE

• The Himalayas are divided into Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser/Middle) and Shiwalik (Outer) ranges; most hill stations, including Ranikhet, lie in the Himachal (Lesser Himalaya) range.

question: In badminton, how high above the ground is the net positioned at the edges?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 5.1 feet.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In badminton, the net is 1.55 metres (about 5 feet 1 inch ≈ 5.1 feet) high at the edges (posts) and 1.524 metres (5 feet) high at the centre. (बैडमिंटन नेट — किनारों पर 5.1 फीट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• A badminton court is 13.4 m long and 6.1 m wide (for doubles); the shuttlecock has 16 feathers.

• Badminton is governed by the Badminton World Federation (BWF), headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

• Famous Indian shuttlers: Prakash Padukone, Pullela Gopichand, Saina Nehwal, P. V. Sindhu (Olympic silver 2016 and bronze 2021), Kidambi Srikanth, Lakshya Sen, and the doubles pair Satwiksairaj Rankireddy–Chirag Shetty.

NOTE

• Major badminton trophies: Thomas Cup (men's teams — India won in 2022), Uber Cup (women's teams), Sudirman Cup (mixed teams).

question: ‘Running for My Life: One Lost Boy’s Journey from the Killing Fields of Sudan to the Olympic Games’ an autobiography depicting the struggle for life to success in life is written by who among the following personalities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lopez Lomong.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Running for My Life: One Lost Boy's Journey from the Killing Fields of Sudan to the Olympic Games" is the autobiography of "Lopez Lomong", a Sudanese-born American track and field (middle-distance) runner. (लोपेज़ लोमोंग की आत्मकथा)

• Lomong was one of the "Lost Boys of Sudan" — children displaced by the Sudanese civil war — who later became a US Olympian and was the US flag-bearer at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Noah Lyles — American sprinter, 100 m Olympic champion (Paris 2024) and multiple world champion.

• Jesse Owens — American athlete who won 4 gold medals at the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

• Arnold Palmer — legendary American golfer.

NOTE

• Famous sports autobiographies: Playing It My Way (Sachin Tendulkar), Ace Against Odds (Sania Mirza), The Test of My Life (Yuvraj Singh), A Shot at History (Abhinav Bindra).

question: Vangpui Kut festival is organised for _______ days in Mizoram to celebrate the glory of Mizo culture and traditions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Vangpui Kut" festival is organised for 2 days in Mizoram to celebrate and showcase the glory of Mizo culture and traditions — folk dances, music, traditional attire and cuisine. (मिज़ोरम का वांगपुई कुट उत्सव — 2 दिन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Kut" means festival in the Mizo language. The major traditional festivals of Mizoram are Chapchar Kut (spring festival, most famous), Mim Kut (maize festival) and Pawl Kut (harvest festival).

• The famous bamboo dance of Mizoram is "Cheraw".

NOTE

• Mizoram: capital — Aizawl; it attained statehood in 1987 (53rd Amendment) as the 23rd state of India. North-East festivals often asked in SSC: Hornbill (Nagaland), Losar (Arunachal/Ladakh), Wangala (Meghalaya), Bihu (Assam).

question: Which of the following represents the chemical formula for sulphur hexafluoride?
solution_text:
The correct answer is SF6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sulphur hexafluoride" has the chemical formula "SF₆" — one sulphur atom bonded to six fluorine atoms ("hexa" = six). (सल्फर हेक्साफ्लोराइड — SF₆)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• SF₆ is a colourless, odourless, non-flammable, inert gas, widely used as an electrical insulator in high-voltage switchgear, circuit breakers and transformers.

• It is one of the most potent greenhouse gases (global warming potential thousands of times higher than CO₂) and is covered under the Kyoto Protocol.

• The molecule has an octahedral shape (sp³d² hybridisation).

NOTE

• Prefixes in chemical names: mono (1), di (2), tri (3), tetra (4), penta (5), hexa (6) — e.g., CO₂ (carbon dioxide), CCl₄ (carbon tetrachloride), SF₆ (sulphur hexafluoride).

question: Which type of tea in large amount is exported from India to importing countries?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Black tea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India exports mainly "black tea" — it constitutes the bulk (around 90%) of India's tea exports, including the famous Assam, Darjeeling and Nilgiri teas. (भारत का प्रमुख चाय निर्यात — काली चाय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India is among the world's largest producers of tea (second after China); Assam is the largest tea-producing state, followed by West Bengal (Darjeeling) and Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris).

• Darjeeling tea was the first Indian product to get the GI (Geographical Indication) tag (2004-05).

• Tea grows well in hot, humid climates with well-drained loamy soil on hill slopes; the Tea Board of India is headquartered in Kolkata.

NOTE

• Types of tea come from the same plant (*Camellia sinensis*) but differ in processing: black tea (fully fermented/oxidised), green tea (unfermented), oolong (partially fermented).

question: The founder of Bahmani kingdom who assumed the title of ‘Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah’ was _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hasan Gangu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bahmani kingdom (1347) was founded by "Hasan Gangu" (Zafar Khan), who assumed the title "Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah". He revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and established the kingdom in the Deccan with its capital at Gulbarga (Ahsanabad). (बहमनी साम्राज्य के संस्थापक — हसन गंगू)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The capital was later shifted from Gulbarga to Bidar by Ahmad Shah Wali.

• Firoz Shah Bahmani (1397–1422) was a learned Bahmani sultan; Mahmud Gawan was the famous Persian minister (wazir) under Muhammad Shah III, known for his madarsa at Bidar.

• The Bahmani kingdom's constant rival was the Vijayanagara Empire (founded 1336 by Harihara and Bukka), with the Raichur Doab as the bone of contention.

NOTE

• After its disintegration (c. 1518–27), the Bahmani kingdom split into the five Deccan Sultanates: Ahmadnagar (Nizam Shahi), Bijapur (Adil Shahi), Golconda (Qutb Shahi), Berar (Imad Shahi) and Bidar (Barid Shahi).

question: Who among the following musicians was a member of Navratnas of Akbar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tansen" (Ramtanu Pandey), the legendary classical musician, was one of the Navratnas (nine gems) of Emperor Akbar's court. Akbar conferred on him the title "Mian". (तानसेन — अकबर के नवरत्न)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar's Navratnas: Tansen, Birbal, Abul Fazl, Faizi, Raja Todar Mal, Raja Man Singh, Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana, Fakir Aziao-Din and Mullah Do-Piyaza.

• Tansen is associated with ragas like Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Todi and Darbari Kanada; his tomb is at Gwalior, where the Tansen Music Festival is held annually.

• Amir Khusrau was the famous poet-musician of the Delhi Sultanate (disciple of Sufi saint Nizamuddin Auliya), credited with developing qawwali and (traditionally) the sitar/tabla — but he lived long before Akbar.

NOTE

• Tansen learnt music from Swami Haridas and was earlier at the court of Raja Ramchandra of Rewa before joining Akbar's court.

question: Kudumbashree is a poverty eradication and women empowerment programme. In which state of India does this programme operate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kudumbashree" is the poverty eradication and women empowerment programme of the Government of Kerala, launched in 1998. The name means "prosperity of the family" in Malayalam. (कुडुम्बश्री — केरल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kudumbashree is implemented through a three-tier structure of Neighbourhood Groups (NHGs), Area Development Societies (ADS) and Community Development Societies (CDS), and is one of the largest women's self-help networks in the world.

• It works with local self-governments (Panchayati Raj institutions) on micro-finance, micro-enterprises, agriculture and social development.

NOTE

• Related national programmes: DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana — National Rural Livelihoods Mission) promotes women SHGs across India; Kudumbashree serves as its State Rural Livelihoods Mission in Kerala.

question: Which Indian classical dance form has composition in Meitei language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Manipuri" classical dance (of Manipur) has compositions in the "Meitei" language (and also in Sanskrit/Brajabhasha for Vaishnava themes). (मणिपुरी नृत्य — मैतेई भाषा)

• Manipuri dance is devotional, centred on Radha-Krishna Raas Leela, with gentle, graceful, rounded movements; the drum used is the Pung (Pung Cholom dance).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sattriya — classical dance of Assam, founded by the Vaishnava saint Srimanta Sankaradeva (compositions in Assamese/Brajavali).

• Chhau — a semi-classical/martial folk dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal (Seraikella, Mayurbhanj, Purulia styles); it is not among the eight classical dances.

• Bharatanatyam — Tamil Nadu; compositions mainly in Tamil/Telugu/Sanskrit.

NOTE

• The Meitei (Manipuri) language is included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution (added by the 71st Amendment, 1992). Famous Manipuri exponents: the Jhaveri sisters, Guru Bipin Singh.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true about the Iron Age?

1 The establishment of large cities took place on the basis of sizeable surplus.

2 The ceramic associated with this age was Painted Grey Ware.

3 The Indus Valley Civilization flourished during the Iron Age
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 — True: In the Iron Age, iron tools (ploughshares, axes) enabled forest clearance and better cultivation, producing a sizeable agricultural surplus, which supported the second urbanisation — the rise of large cities in the Ganga valley (c. 6th century BCE) and the Mahajanapadas.

• Statement 2 — True: The characteristic pottery/ceramic of the early Iron Age in northern India was "Painted Grey Ware (PGW)" (c. 1200–600 BCE), followed by the Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW).

• Statement 3 — False: The Indus Valley Civilization (c. 2600–1900 BCE) was a Bronze Age (Chalcolithic) civilisation — the Harappans did not know iron.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Iron use in India began around 1200–1000 BCE, associated with the Later Vedic period; important early iron sites: Atranjikhera, Hastinapur (UP).

• Sequence of ages: Stone Age → Chalcolithic/Bronze Age → Iron Age.

NOTE

• The first urbanisation = Harappan cities (Bronze Age); the second urbanisation = Ganga valley cities of the 6th century BCE (Iron Age, NBPW period).
